question.problem:
Consider the inhomogeneous system  ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)+g(t),$ where $A$ is a constant square matrix. A derivation of the formula for the solution $x(t)$ passing through $x({t}_{0})$ is presented below.

$\text{L1}:\,$ Let $y(t)={e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}x(t)$  

$\text{L2}:\,$ ${y}^{′}(t)=-A{e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}x(t)+{e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}{x}^{′}(t)$  

$\text{L3}:\,$ ${y}^{′}(t)={e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}g(t)$  

$\text{L4}:\,$ $y(t)-y({t}_{0})={\int }_{{t}_{0}}^{t}{e}^{-A(s-{t}_{0})}g(s)\,\text{d}s$

$\text{L5}:\,$ $y({t}_{0})=x({t}_{0})$ 

$\text{L6}:\,$ $y(t)=x({t}_{0})+{\int }_{{t}_{0}}^{t}{e}^{-A(s-{t}_{0})}g(s)\,\text{d}s$  

$\text{L7}:\,$ ${e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}y(t)={e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}x({t}_{0})+{\int }_{{t}_{0}}^{t}{e}^{A(t-s)}g(s)\,\text{d}s$

$\text{L8}:\,$ ${e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}y(t)=x(t)$

$\text{L9}:\,$ $x(t)={e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}x({t}_{0})+{\int }_{{t}_{0}}^{t}{e}^{A(t-s)}g(s)\,\text{d}s$

Select the correct options to justify each step of the reasoning.

$\,$ Line $\text{L3}$ follows from $\text{L2}$ by  
{{field-1}}.

$\,$ Line $\text{L5}$ follows from line $\text{L1}$ by  
{{field-2}}.

$\,$ Line $\text{L7}$ follows from line $\text{L6}$ by  
{{field-3}}.
question.worked_solution:
Let's justify each of the selected steps.

- We first consider lines $\text{L2}$ and $\text{L3}.$ Starting from

$$
{y}^{′}(t)=-A{e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}x(t)+{e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}{x}^{′}(t)
$$

in $\text{L2}$ and substituting ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)+g(t)$ from the original system gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(t) & =-A{e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}x(t)+{e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}(Ax(t)+g(t)) \\  & =-A{e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}x(t)+A{e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}x(t)+{e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}g(t) \\  & ={e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}g(t).\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, $\text{L3}$ follows from $\text{L2}$ by $\text{substituting }{x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)+g(t).$

- Next, we consider lines $\text{L1}$ and $\text{L5}.$ Evaluating $y(t)={e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}x(t)$ at $t={t}_{0}$ gives

$$
y({t}_{0})={e}^{-A({t}_{0}-{t}_{0})}x({t}_{0})=Ix({t}_{0})=x({t}_{0}).
$$

Therefore, $\text{L5}$ follows from $\text{L1}$ by $\text{evaluating at }t={t}_{0}.$

- Finally, we consider lines $\text{L6}$ and $\text{L7}.$ Multiplying both sides of

$$
y(t)=x({t}_{0})+{\int }_{{t}_{0}}^{t}{e}^{-A(s-{t}_{0})}g(s)\,ds
$$

from $\text{L6}$ by ${e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}y(t) & ={e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}x({t}_{0})+{e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}{\int }_{{t}_{0}}^{t}{e}^{-A(s-{t}_{0})}g(s)\,\text{d}s \\  & ={e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}x({t}_{0})+{\int }_{{t}_{0}}^{t}{e}^{A(t-s)}g(s)\,\text{d}s.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\text{L7}$ follows from $\text{L6}$ by $\text{multiplying both sides by }{e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}.$
